Order 
This is the s e c o n d bail application filed on behalf of the applicant/accused under Section 482 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Surksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of anticipatory bail, as he is under apprehension of his arrest, in connection with Crime No.161/2024, registered at Police Station Dehat District Tikamgarh (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471/34 of the IPC.
2. Learned senior counsel appearing for applicant submitted that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
There was commercial transaction between applicant and complainant.
Civil suit for recovery of money has also been filed against complainant.
Applicant will not abscond from law and he will cooperate in investigation of case.

In these circumstances,
applicant be released on anticipatory bail.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:40377 2 MCRC-31277-2024 3.
Learned Govt. Advocate appearing for the State as well as counsel appearing for objector opposed the application for grant of anticipatory bail.

It is submitted that offence is serious in nature and Jamna Prasad Asati vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109251791/
1 railway receipts have been forged.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applicant by practicing forgery and cheating has misappropriated an amount of Rs.3.20/- crores from them.
In these circumstances, applicant may not be granted anticipatory bail.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
5.
First application filed by applicant was dismissed as withdrawn.
Offence is serious in nature.
Forgery is said to have been committed by applicant and as per investigation agency, railway receipts are forged and no supply has been made.
6. Considering totality the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that it is not a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail.
Accordingly, bail application is dismissed.
(VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE pn
